# Commands

<!-- Generated by `mise run docs:commands`: this intro from docs/commands-intro.md, the list from the task
descriptions in tasks/*.toml and mise.toml. Edit those, not this file. -->

Every command is a mise task: `mise run <task>`; `mise tasks` lists them. Which to use when:

- **Develop:** `dev`: the real Worker runtime (Intl, board, D1, Durable Objects) on workerd, rebuilt on every save
  with the fast `build:dev`.
- **Build:** `build` is production (what ships and what the tests use), compiled by `WORKER_COMPILER` in mise.toml:
  `tinygo` (smallest wasm, ~1–2 min builds) or `go` (seconds, a bigger wasm, ~50–90 ms slower per request).
  Override it for one run: `WORKER_COMPILER=go mise run check`. `build:dev` is always standard Go, for `dev`.
- **Test:** `check` before pushing (CI runs the same, `charter ci run` from `charter.toml`'s `[ci]`), then
  `e2e` for anything in the browser.
  `SMOKE_BASE=https://… smoke` runs the smoke checks against a deployed Worker.
- **Ship:** every pushed branch gets a preview and `main` deploys staging, both automatically (Workers Builds).
  Production: `release v1.3` (or a v* tag from GitHub's Releases page) → CI tests it and tags it → Workers Builds
  deploys it, with no Cloudflare credentials anywhere but Cloudflare. `deploy` does it by hand from a machine with fnox credentials.
  All of them are `charter deploy` with `charter.toml`: [deploy.md](deploy.md).

## Tasks

### `assets`

- Depends: vendor, gsxkit:add, gsxui:css

- **Usage:** `assets`

Assemble dist/site, the Static Assets for workerd and deploy: htmx, intl's browser module, gsxui's behaviours, gsxkit's components' browser files, CSS and fonts

### `bench`

- Depends: build

- **Usage:** `bench`

CPU per request of the production build on local workerd, per page, repeated runs (charter bench)

### `bench:variants`

- Depends: generate, assets

- **Usage:** `bench:variants`

Build the current code with each of charter's optimisations off in turn, measure each, write docs/benchmarks.md

### `build`

- Depends: generate, assets

- **Usage:** `build`

Production build → build/ with WORKER_COMPILER (mise.toml: tinygo or go), size-checked (deploy, staging, CI and the tests use it)

### `build:dev`

- Depends: generate, assets

- **Usage:** `build:dev`

Dev build → build/: standard Go to wasm, seconds after an edit (mise run dev uses it; never deployed)

### `charter:build`

- **Usage:** `charter:build`

Build the Worker into build/ (charter build): a Go one with TinyGo (WORKER_COMPILER=go: the standard compiler, in seconds, never to deploy), a TypeScript one bundled with esbuild

### `charter:builds-configure`

- **Usage:** `charter:builds-configure`

Set Workers Builds up for the Worker: the repository, .mise/tasks/charter-builds as its build and deploy commands (charter builds configure; Cloudflare credentials)

### `charter:check`

- **Usage:** `charter:check`

Every check that needs no Cloudflare account (charter check): charter's files, and a project's types, specs, tests and Worker; exits 1 on any problem

### `charter:ci`

A job of charter.toml's [ci.jobs] here, as GitHub runs it (charter ci <job>); none: every job run on a change, or an app's own [ci] (charter ci run)


- **Usage:** `charter:ci [job] [project]`

### Arguments
- **`[job]`** — a job of charter.toml's [ci.jobs]
- **`[project]`** — the project to run it in, for a job that runs in each

### `charter:deploy`

Deploy the built Worker to production, staging or a preview <name>, as charter.toml says (charter deploy); prints its URL


- **Usage:** `charter:deploy <environment> [name]`

### Arguments
- **`<environment>`** — production, staging or preview
- **`[name]`** — the preview's name, e.g. pr-7

### `charter:dev`

- **Usage:** `charter:dev`

Build the Worker and run it on local workerd, on charter.toml's port, until Ctrl-C (charter dev)

### `charter:docs`

- **Usage:** `charter:docs`

After changing a page in docs/: what a program can see wrong in it (charter docs)

### `charter:init`

- **Usage:** `charter:init`

After upgrading charter: charter's files, these tasks, the skill and the workflows again (charter init)

### `charter:issues`

First, whenever you start: the open issues (charter issues); with a kind (bug, feature, upstream, plan), a new one's body and the gh command that files it


- **Usage:** `charter:issues [kind]`

### Arguments
- **`[kind]`** — bug, feature, upstream or plan

### `charter:live-test`

- **Usage:** `charter:live-test`

The standard test and charter.toml's [test] live against the deployed Worker (charter live-test)

### `charter:repo`

- **Usage:** `charter:repo`

After changing charter.toml's [github]: the repo on GitHub as it says (charter repo)

### `charter:sdk`

An SDK with Fern (Docker) into sdk/out, by default the TypeScript one (charter sdk; charter sdk -prove proves every client, -publish commits the Go SDK)


- **Usage:** `charter:sdk [group]`

### Arguments
- **`[group]`** — a group of fern/generators.yml, e.g. python

### `charter:serve`

- **Usage:** `charter:serve`

Run the built Worker on local workerd, on charter.toml's port (PORT overrides it), in your time zone (charter serve)

### `charter:skill`

- **Usage:** `charter:skill`

After upgrading charter: its agent skill again, into .claude/skills/charter (charter skill)

### `charter:spec`

- **Usage:** `charter:spec`

After changing the contract, [sdks] or migrations/: both specs from the contract, Fern's settings and the database's code (charter spec)

### `charter:tail`

- **Usage:** `charter:tail`

Stream the deployed Worker's live logs until Ctrl-C (charter tail)

### `charter:tasks`

- **Usage:** `charter:tasks`

After upgrading charter: these tasks and the Workers Builds launcher again (charter tasks)

### `charter:token`

- **Usage:** `charter:token`

Check the Cloudflare token is active (charter token)

### `charter:upstream`

- **Usage:** `charter:upstream`

Now and then: the upstream issues the code works around, and their state (charter upstream)

### `charter:with`

Run a command against the built Worker on local workerd, a free port and fresh state, BASE its URL (charter with)


- **Usage:** `charter:with <command>…`

### Arguments
- **`<command>…`** — the command and its arguments

### `charter:workflow`

- **Usage:** `charter:workflow`

After upgrading charter: the CI workflow again, .github/workflows/charter.yml (charter workflow)

### `ci:bench`

- Depends: build

- **Usage:** `ci:bench`

CI: one short CPU-per-request run of the build on workerd, into the GitHub run's summary (charter.toml [ci] test)

### `deploy`

- Depends: test, token-check

- **Usage:** `deploy`

Test, then deploy production → https://$APP_DOMAIN (or $APP_NAME.&lt;subdomain>.workers.dev), then seo:audit live

### `dev`

- **Usage:** `dev`

gsx dev → build:dev (standard Go, seconds) + CSS → workerd restart on every .gsx/.go save → http://localhost:8913 (PORT: another port)

### `docs:commands`

- **Usage:** `docs:commands`

Regenerate docs/commands.md from these task descriptions (mise generate task-docs); test:go fails when it's stale

### `e2e`

- Depends: build

- **Usage:** `e2e`

Headless Chrome checks: pages, live board in two browsers, boost ↔ board, presence, Intl, write limit (local workerd, or E2E_BASE=https://…)

### `fresh`

- **Usage:** `fresh`

Brand-new gsx apps outside this repo (e2e/fresh): one made from intl's and seo's READMEs (every go and gsx block in them is its code), with gsxui and intl's screens, on an ordinary Go server in English and German, its go test, seo:audit and intl:check passing; and one on Workers set up with charter init, its go test on charter's stand-ins and its Worker on local workerd (FRESH_DEPLOY=1: on Cloudflare too)

### `fresh:published`

- **Usage:** `fresh:published`

The fresh-app test with intl and seo as published on the Go proxy (@latest), not this checkout: after a release, once the proxy has its tags, it shows the READMEs work for someone who runs go get

### `generate`

- Depends: intl, gsx:generate

- **Usage:** `generate`

gsx:generate for the app, intl's and seo's own components (their modules commit them for the apps that import them), and structpages' tables for TinyGo

### `gsx:editor`

- **Usage:** `gsx:editor`

Install go.mod's gsx into GOPATH/bin for the VS Code gsx language server

### `gsx:fmt`

Format every .gsx file with gsx fmt; --check lists what isn't formatted and fails, writing nothing (for CI)


- **Usage:** `gsx:fmt [--check]`

### Flags
- **`--check`** — fail on an unformatted file, writing nothing

### `gsx:generate`

- **Usage:** `gsx:generate`

go tool gsx generate: every .gsx file to its .x.go (after intl, when intl is running too: views write its messages)

### `gsx:skill`

- **Usage:** `gsx:skill`

Install or update the agent skills Jackie Li's projects ship (gsx's, structpages', gsxui's), at the versions the app pins (go.mod, mise.toml), into .claude/skills

### `gsx:tasks`

- **Usage:** `gsx:tasks`

Write this file again from the gsxkit version in go.mod: run it after upgrading gsxkit

### `gsx:update`

- **Usage:** `gsx:update`

gsx, gsxui and structpages to their latest (go tool gsxkit update), except what deps.toml holds; the tasks, skills, generated code and copies follow

### `gsxkit:add`

- Depends: gsxkit:bundle

- **Usage:** `gsxkit:add`

Copy gsxkit's map and moq components into the app with go tool gsxkit add -overwrite: views/gsxkit, web/gsxkit and their text (after gsxkit:bundle)

### `gsxkit:bundle`

- **Usage:** `gsxkit:bundle`

Bundle gsxkit's components' browser files (the map's Leaflet, the live video's @moq elements, each with its glue) from the npm packages each npm-lock.json pins, into gsxkit/ui/assets (no Node)

### `gsxkit:update`

Re-resolve a gsxkit component's npm packages (e.g. mise run gsxkit:update moq @moq/watch@0.6.6 @moq/publish@0.5.3, or map leaflet@1.9.4), rewrite its npm-lock.json and bundle; @moq stays at a version Cloudflare's relays speak until they ship draft-18 (#158)


- **Usage:** `gsxkit:update <component> <packages>…`

### Arguments
- **`<component>`** — map or moq
- **`<packages>…`** — name@version of each package to resolve

### `gsxui:css`

gsxui's CSS: its entry (gsxui.json's css) compiled by the standalone Tailwind CLI, into dist/gsxui.css by default


- **Usage:** `gsxui:css [out]`

### Arguments
- **`[out]`** — the compiled file

  **Default:** `dist/gsxui.css`

### `gsxui:theme`

Switch the app's look to a gsxui theme with gsxui apply: a style's standard theme by name (nova, gsxui's default; vega, maia, lyra, mira, luma, sera, rhea), or any share code from gsxui's theme editor (https://ui.gsxhq.dev/theme). Then commit what it changed


- **Usage:** `gsxui:theme <theme>`

### Arguments
- **`<theme>`** — a style (nova, vega, maia, lyra, mira, luma, sera, rhea) or a gsxui:p1:… share code

### `intl`

- **Usage:** `intl`

Compile the catalogs (intl.toml): the Go package of messages, intl-messages.mjs, the gsxui translator, intl.sum and the languages badge (intl.toml's badge); a language just added to intl.toml's locales gets its catalog. Run it after editing a catalog; gsx generate needs it first

### `intl:add`

Copy intl's screens into the app the way gsxui add copies components: language-list, language-offer, preferences (gsx files in intl.toml's ui, made of gsxui components, their text already translated into the catalogs). --diff shows how the app's copies differ; --overwrite replaces copies the app changed


- **Usage:** `intl:add [--diff] [--overwrite] <screen>…`

### Arguments
- **`<screen>…`** — language-list, language-offer or preferences

### Flags
- **`--diff`** — show how intl's screens differ from the app's copies, writing nothing (exit 1 if they do)
- **`--overwrite`** — replace copies the app changed

### `intl:add-locale`

Add a language: its id as Intl writes it (fr-ca → fr-CA) into intl.toml's locales, and its catalog; then mise run intl:translate


- **Usage:** `intl:add-locale <locale>…`

### Arguments
- **`<locale>…`** — BCP 47 ids, e.g. fr or pt-BR

### `intl:check`

- **Usage:** `intl:check`

Every problem, for CI: the catalogs (ICU syntax, arguments, a case for each plural category Intl says a language uses, missing and stale translations, unused messages, gsxui text, intl.sum), then gsx's own checks on the app's markup (gsx generate, gsx fmt, the gsx skill's find-smells.sh); exits 1 on any

### `intl:confirm`

Keep stale translations as they are: the source changed, their meaning didn't (a typo fixed). All of them, or only some: de, or de:board.notes


- **Usage:** `intl:confirm [which]…`

### Arguments
- **`[which]…`** — de, or de:board.notes (default: every stale translation)

### `intl:export`

XLIFF 2.0 per locale into xliff/out (intl.toml's xliff), for human translators and translation-management systems: what is left to translate (--all: every message)


- **Usage:** `intl:export [--all] [locale]…`

### Arguments
- **`[locale]…`** — only these locales (default: all)

### Flags
- **`--all`** — every message, not only what is left

### `intl:import`

Read translators' XLIFF 2.0 back into the catalogs, each target checked against its source: every file in xliff/in, or the ones named; then compile


- **Usage:** `intl:import [file]…`

### Arguments
- **`[file]…`** — &lt;locale>.xlf files (default: every file in xliff/in)

### `intl:prune`

- **Usage:** `intl:prune`

Remove from every catalog the keys the source no longer has (intl:check names them)

### `intl:skill`

- **Usage:** `intl:skill`

Install or update the intl agent skill (.claude/skills/intl), which Claude Code uses to write and translate the app's text

### `intl:status`

- **Usage:** `intl:status`

Per locale: translated, inherited, stale and missing messages; exits 1 when a locale is incomplete

### `intl:tasks`

- **Usage:** `intl:tasks`

Write this file again from the intl version in go.mod: run it after upgrading intl (intl:check says when)

### `intl:todo`

What is left to translate, per locale: each message's source, context and arguments, the plural categories the language needs, the style note (--json for agents)


- **Usage:** `intl:todo [--json] [locale]…`

### Arguments
- **`[locale]…`** — only these locales (default: all)

### Flags
- **`--json`** — JSON on stdout, for agents

### `intl:translate`

Translate every missing and stale message with Claude Code (the intl skill), one worker per language at once (intl.toml [translate]), until intl:check passes. Needs claude on PATH


- **Usage:** `intl:translate [locale]…`

### Arguments
- **`[locale]…`** — only these locales (default: all)

### `load`

- Depends: build

- **Usage:** `load`

1,000 WebSockets in every locale on one topic, a 50-write burst, socket 1,001 refused (e2e/load; local workerd, or LOAD_BASE=https://…)

### `outdated`

- **Usage:** `outdated`

Every pin with a newer version upstream (Go modules in every module, mise's tools, gsxui's commit, Chrome, htmx, the npm locks), deps.toml's holds marked

### `preview`

Test, then deploy a Worker Preview named after the branch (or e.g. pr-7) → its URL on stdout and in .preview-url


- Depends: test

- **Usage:** `preview [name]`

### Arguments
- **`[name]`** — preview name, e.g. pr-7; the branch unless named

### `release`

Release main to production (e.g. v1.3): CI tests it, tags it (and intl/seo with their next version when they changed), Workers Builds deploys it; no Cloudflare credentials needed


- **Usage:** `release <version>`

### Arguments
- **`<version>`** — the release, e.g. v1.3

### `seo:audit`

Fetch robots.txt and every sitemap URL live as Googlebot: 200, indexable, self-canonical, lang, title, description, one h1, reciprocal hreflang (no Google account needed)


- **Usage:** `seo:audit [--json]`

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout

### `seo:badges`

- **Usage:** `seo:badges`

Lighthouse on every page and the audit, then the README's badges (seo.toml's [badges] dir: each Lighthouse category's lowest page, the audit) and its &lt;!-- seo:scores --> table; run after a production release, then commit

### `seo:inspect`

One URL (the home page unless named): Google's verdict, last crawl and canonical, and the link to its Search Console page


- Depends: seo:access

- **Usage:** `seo:inspect [--json] [--open] [page]`

### Arguments
- **`[page]`** — a path like /de/ or a full URL

  **Default:** `/`

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout
- **`--open`** — open its Search Console page (Test live URL, Request indexing)

### `seo:lighthouse`

Lighthouse on the live site, on Google's servers through PageSpeed Insights: every page of the sitemap (seo.toml's pages), or one; performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO out of 100, what fails and on which elements, real users' Core Web Vitals; fails under seo.toml's min (90)


- **Usage:** `seo:lighthouse [--json] [--desktop] [page]`

### Arguments
- **`[page]`** — one page, a path like /de/board or a full URL; default every page

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout
- **`--desktop`** — score the desktop page instead of the mobile one Google indexes

### `seo:setup`

- **Usage:** `seo:setup`

Once: the Google Cloud project, the Search Console and PageSpeed Insights APIs, and a service account key in fnox (needs gcloud auth login)

### `seo:sites`

The Search Console properties the service account can use; fails without Full access


- **Usage:** `seo:sites [--json]`

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout

### `seo:skill`

- **Usage:** `seo:skill`

Install or update the seo agent skill (.claude/skills/seo), which Claude Code uses to check and fix how Google sees the site

### `seo:status`

The sitemap's status in Search Console and Google's index status for every URL in it


- Depends: seo:access

- **Usage:** `seo:status [--json]`

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout

### `seo:submit`

- Depends: seo:access, seo:audit

- **Usage:** `seo:submit`

Submit the site's sitemap.xml (seo.toml's site) to Search Console, after access and a passing live audit

### `seo:tasks`

- **Usage:** `seo:tasks`

Write this file again from the seo version in go.mod: run it after upgrading seo

### `seo:todo`

Google's verdict for every sitemap URL (indexed, waiting, duplicate, problem); fails on problems


- Depends: seo:access

- **Usage:** `seo:todo [--json] [--open]`

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout
- **`--open`** — open Google's page for each problem (Test live URL, Request indexing)

### `serve`

- Depends: build

- **Usage:** `serve`

The production build (WORKER_COMPILER) on local workerd (charter serve: charter.toml's port, your time zone), static files first → http://localhost:8913

### `smoke`

- Depends: build

- **Usage:** `smoke`

The production build on local workerd, every route checked over HTTP (e2e/smoke); SMOKE_BASE=https://… checks a deployed Worker

### `staging`

- Depends: test

- **Usage:** `staging`

Test, then deploy staging: the Worker $APP_NAME-staging → its URL on stdout and in .staging-url

### `structpages:lint`

- **Usage:** `structpages:lint`

structpages-lint over the app: URLs, ids and partials against the page tree, internal URLs written as strings, htmx without a target selector; exit 1 on a finding

### `tail`

- **Usage:** `tail`

Stream the deployed Worker's live logs (requests, console, exceptions) → Ctrl-C to stop

### `test`

- Depends: smoke, test:go, fresh

- **Usage:** `test`
- **Aliases:** `check`

Everything before a push: the production build + workerd smoke, gsx fmt/gofmt, go vet, go test, the fresh-app test (mise run check is the same)

### `test:go`

- Depends: generate

- **Usage:** `test:go`

Every module's go.mod tidy, gsx fmt/gofmt check + go vet + structpages-lint + go test, the app and its modules: intl/, seo/, badge/, gsxkit/ (standard Go; runs beside the production build)

### `token-check`

- **Usage:** `token-check`

Verify CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (from fnox) against the Cloudflare API (charter token)

### `update`

- **Usage:** `update`

Move every pin not held in deps.toml to its latest (go tool gsxkit update, then Go modules, mise's tools and their copies, charter with charter init, Chrome, htmx, the npm locks), tidy every module, regenerate, then check and e2e

### `upstream:branch`

A new branch in an upstream checkout, from upstream's current main


- **Usage:** `upstream:branch <repo> <name>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages
- **`<name>`** — the branch, e.g. docs-calendar-from-cldr

### `upstream:check`

An upstream checkout's Go checks with its own pinned Go (gsx generate/fmt, its own check commands, vet, test), no npm; a failing package is re-run on upstream's main and reported as already failing there or new


- **Usage:** `upstream:check <repo>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages

### `upstream:fork`

Create your fork of an upstream project on GitHub and add it as the checkout's origin


- **Usage:** `upstream:fork <repo>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages

### `upstream:review`

An upstream checkout's commits and diff against upstream's main, to read before anything is sent


- **Usage:** `upstream:review <repo>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages

### `upstream:status`

- **Usage:** `upstream:status`

Every upstream checkout (gsx, gsxui, structpages): where it is on disk, its branch, local changes, how your fork's main differs

### `upstream:sync`

Clone or fetch the upstream checkouts (all, or one), adding your fork as origin when you have one; never pushes


- **Usage:** `upstream:sync [repo]`

### Arguments
- **`[repo]`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages (default: all)

### `upstream:tinygo`

An upstream package's own tests compiled by this repo's TinyGo: whether it runs where Workers builds run (e.g. reflect)


- **Usage:** `upstream:tinygo <repo> [package]`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages
- **`[package]`** — a package pattern in the checkout (default ./...)

### `upstream:unuse`

Back to the pinned version of an upstream project after upstream:use


- **Usage:** `upstream:unuse <repo>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages

### `upstream:use`

Build and test this app with an upstream checkout instead of the pinned version (go.work for a Go module; gsxui re-vendored by the checkout's CLI). mise run check fails until upstream:unuse


- **Usage:** `upstream:use <repo>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages

### `vendor`

- **Usage:** `vendor`

Vendor htmx 4.0.0 htmx.min.js + ext/hx-ws.js + ext/hx-live.js into web/htmx/ (curl, integrity-checked)
